tests.title: The 'no work without a task' gate blocks and allows the right files
tests.description: Checks the safeguard that stops project files from being changed when no work task is active. Protected files must be blocked; everyday exempt files (task notes, settings) must still be allowed.
tests.approach: Runs the gate's own 63-scenario self-test in a clean environment: it simulates edit attempts with and without an active task and compares every block/allow decision against the expected one. Passes only when the suite reports all scenarios passed.
tests.judged_by: output must contain "ALL TESTS PASSED" and exit code 0

tests.title: The document-conversion gate stops uncontrolled conversions
tests.cmd: bash -c export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$PWD"; H=.claude/skills/docflow/hooks/block-direct-conversion.sh; if [ -f .state/docflow-active ]; then echo 'bypass marker present - gate cannot be exercised'; exit 1; fi; printf '%s' '{"tool_input":{"command":"pandoc report.docx -o report.md"}}' | bash "$H" 2>/dev/null; d=$?; printf '%s' '{"tool_input":{"command":"ls docs"}}' | bash "$H" 2>/dev/null; a=$?; echo "deny_exit=$d allow_exit=$a"; [ "$d" -eq 2 ] && [ "$a" -eq 0 ]
tests.description: Checks the safeguard that prevents documents from being converted outside the controlled pipeline (which preserves images, structure, and traceability).
tests.approach: Feeds the gate two simulated commands: a direct document conversion (must be refused) and a harmless file listing (must be permitted), then verifies both decisions came back exactly as required.

tests.title: Auto-generated document sections stay faithful and do no harm
tests.description: Checks the machinery that fills in auto-generated tables and trees inside project documents: generated content must always match the source of truth, and text written by hand around it must never be touched.
tests.approach: Runs the generator's regression suite: it renders known inputs repeatedly and verifies the output is identical every time (idempotent), preserves hand-written content, and refuses unsafe targets.

tests.title: Advisor grounding files are built correctly
tests.description: Checks the machinery that prepares each AI advisor's reading list (the project documents it grounds its answers in), so advisors always cite from the right sources.
tests.approach: Runs the advisor tooling's regression suite: it builds grounding blocks from known configurations and verifies the generated lists, file wiring, and search integration match the expected output.

tests.title: Writing-quality checks catch known defects
tests.description: Checks the automatic proof-reading tools that flag clutter, jargon, hedging, and AI-sounding text before a document goes to review.
tests.approach: Runs the lint engines against fixture texts with known, planted defects and verifies each defect is detected and clean text is not flagged.

tests.title: The document-coverage audit finds what's missing
tests.description: Checks the audit that compares the project's document set against the catalog of documents regulations require, so gaps are found by us and not by an auditor.
tests.approach: Runs the audit machinery's 48-scenario self-test: it builds document sets with known gaps and verifies each gap (and each satisfied obligation) is reported correctly.

tests.title: Traceability-chain checks work
tests.description: Checks the tooling that verifies every requirement traces forward to design and tests and backward to user needs — the chain auditors walk.
tests.approach: Runs the trace tooling's regression suite: known trace graphs with deliberate breaks are analyzed and the tool must find every break and confirm intact chains in both directions.

tests.title: Submission-tracker wiring works
tests.description: Checks the dashboard tooling that tracks submission-package readiness, so status shown to the team reflects the real state of the documents.
tests.approach: Runs the tracker's regression suite: builds tracker rows from known inputs and verifies the generated draft-context wiring matches expectations.

tests.title: Jira-drift detection works
tests.cmd: uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml --with openpyxl -- pytest .claude/skills/jira-pull/tests -q --deselect .claude/skills/jira-pull/tests/test_drift_rules.py::test_exec
tests.description: Checks the tooling that compares our requirement matrices against Jira, so silent divergence between the two systems is caught.
tests.approach: Runs the drift-rule suite: feeds known Jira/matrix states containing planted mismatches and verifies every mismatch type is detected (69 checks).

tests.title: Repo-to-formal-systems document transfer is faithful
tests.description: Checks the machinery that moves controlled documents between this repo and the formal systems (Confluence, Google Docs) without corrupting content or losing review state.
tests.approach: Runs the transfer machinery's 139-test suite covering conversion fidelity, review tiers, freeze states, and error handling against known documents.

tests.title: The project console works end to end
tests.description: Checks the team's browser console — the pages, data loaders, and workflows this very Validation view lives in — so what the team sees reflects repo truth.
tests.approach: Runs the console's 83-test suite in its real environment, including end-to-end workflow tests that exercise pages the way a user would.

tests.title: Slide-deck builder keeps content intact
tests.description: Checks the presentation tooling that turns project documents into slide decks without dropping or duplicating content.
tests.approach: Runs the deck builder's regression suite verifying slide identity is preserved across rebuilds.

tests.title: Tool updates never overwrite local improvements
tests.description: Checks the safeguard in the tool-sync machinery: when pulling shared tooling updates, a locally improved file must be flagged for review, never silently replaced.
tests.approach: Runs the sync tool's three-way-merge self-test: it constructs update scenarios (upstream newer, local newer, both changed) and verifies each is classified correctly and no local-ahead file is overwritten.

tests.title: The tool-sync health check reports the truth
tests.description: Checks the at-a-glance status report that tells a team member whether their tools are in step with the team's shared registry.
tests.approach: Runs the status action's self-test against constructed in-sync and out-of-sync states and verifies each is reported correctly.

tests.title: Installed tools pass the security screen
tests.description: Checks that a security scan of every installed tool (skills, agents, hooks, settings) finds no hostile patterns — and that the scanner itself fails loudly when it does.
tests.approach: Runs the security scanner across the whole workbench in machine-readable mode; the case passes only when no Critical or High findings remain undispositioned.

tests.title: Every tool declares its version
tests.cmd: python3 -c import re,sys;from pathlib import Path;EXEMPT={'docx','pdf','pptx','xlsx'};missing=[d.name for d in sorted(Path('.claude/skills').iterdir()) if d.is_dir() and d.name not in EXEMPT and (d/'SKILL.md').is_file() and not (re.search(r'^version:\s*\S+',(d/'SKILL.md').read_text(errors='replace')[:2000],re.M) or (d/'VERSION').is_file())];print('missing version:',missing) if missing else print('all skills versioned (external office skills exempt)');sys.exit(1 if missing else 0)
tests.description: Checks that each installed tool states a version, so the team can always say exactly which tool versions were validated (bundled third-party office tools are exempt).
tests.approach: Sweeps every installed skill and verifies a version declaration exists in its metadata or VERSION file; lists any tool that has none.
